pages.title: Payroll compliance
pages.content: We review one payroll cycle for holiday pay, working time, payslips and year-end, including statutory sick pay and the PRSI and USC set-up with your provider. The review is advisory and covers up to 150 staff. We do not run payroll. Fixed fee €1,900.

pages.title: Policies & handbooks
pages.content: We write an employee handbook of up to 12 policies, in language a manager can apply, covering contracts, leave and remote work. A separate contract set, templates for three role types, is €980 fixed. Handbook fixed fee €2,400.

pages.title: Workplace investigations
pages.content: We take an independent look at one complaint, whether it is a grievance, a disciplinary matter or bullying. Scope is agreed first. We hold up to six interviews and write a findings report, typically within 18 working days of the last interview. From €3,800.

pages.title: Retainer support
pages.content: One adviser stays on the file. Essentials is up to six hours a month at €890. Growth is up to 14 hours a month, plus a quarterly review, at €1,850. We reply within one working day. The minimum term is three months, then monthly.

posts.title: A handbook before the funding round
posts.excerpt: A 60-person software company in Cork asked for a handbook and contracts before a funding round. We rebuilt both in five weeks.
posts.content:
The situation

A 60-person software company in Cork was preparing for a funding round and wanted its handbook and contracts in order first. The existing documents had grown piece by piece, and nobody could say which version applied to whom.

What we did

We agreed a written scope and a fixed fee, read the contracts and policies in use, and rebuilt both: an employee handbook in language a manager can apply, and contract wording to match. A weekly check-in kept the company's own people in the loop.

Where it left them

The work took five weeks, from the agreed scope to the written handover. The company is not named, and we make no claim about the funding round itself; that was theirs. Follow-up questions on the work were included for 30 days.

posts.title: Holiday pay across four sites
posts.excerpt: A 140-person hospitality group ran payroll across four sites. We reviewed one cycle, documented the holiday-pay corrections, and the group paid them.
posts.content:
The situation

A 140-person hospitality group was running payroll across four sites, each with its own way of recording working time and leave. The group wanted to know whether holiday pay was being calculated the same way everywhere.

What we did

We reviewed one payroll cycle with the group's payroll provider: holiday pay, working-time records and payslip content. The review was advisory; we did not run the payroll. We documented each correction in a written report.

Where it left them

The group paid the corrections we documented. That is the whole of what we report. A payroll compliance review is a fixed fee, agreed in writing before the work starts.

posts.title: An independent look at a grievance
posts.excerpt: A 35-person design studio asked for an independent look at a grievance. We agreed a scope, held the interviews and issued the findings report.
posts.content:
The situation

A 35-person design studio had received a grievance and wanted someone outside the team to look at it independently, so that the people involved could trust the process.

What we did

We agreed the scope of the complaint in writing first, then held the interviews and wrote a findings report. Each person was told what the process was and how the report would be used.

Where it left them

The findings report was issued 18 working days after the last interview. The timing in this matter is the timing we record, not a promise for the next one.

posts.title: What a fixed fee covers
posts.excerpt: A fixed fee is tied to a scope written down before we start. Here is what that means for a health check, a handbook and an investigation.
posts.content:
Every fee on this site is in euro and excludes VAT at 23%. The number you accept is tied to a scope written down before the work starts. A change of scope is a new written quote, not an open hourly bill.

An HR health check is €1,450 fixed: contracts, policies and payroll set-up reviewed, with a written report in 10 working days. A payroll compliance review is €1,900 fixed for one payroll cycle and up to 150 staff. An employee handbook is €2,400 fixed for up to 12 policies. An investigation starts from €3,800 for one complaint, up to six interviews and a findings report.

Retainers run at €890 a month for Essentials and €1,850 a month for Growth, with a three-month minimum and then monthly.
